The learned counsels for the petitioner and the State are present.

2. This criminal revision has been filed against the order dated 09.10.2018 passed in ST Case No.344 of 2007 arising out of Kotwali P.S. Case No.434 of 2006 corresponding to GR No.2312 of 2006 registered under section 376 of Indian Penal Code whereby the learned Additional Judicial Commissioner-III, Ranchi has rejected the petition filed by the petitioner on 29.01.2013 wherein the petitioner sought a declaration that he was juvenile.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the learned court did not conduct any inquiry and passed the impugned order.
4. The learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer of the petitioner and has submitted that the specific case of the petitioner that he was born on 05.01.1988.
The impugned order has been passed by taking his date of birth as 05.01.1988 itself.

The learned counsel submits that the learned court has also considered the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and has Aditya Singh @ Bittu Singh @ Bittu Son Of ... vs The State Of Jharkhand on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10544305/

sentences.text: After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and upon going through the impugned order, this Court finds that the petitioner claimed that he was born on 05.01.1988 and taking the said date, the impugned order has been passed and it has been recorded that the duration of the offence was from 14.02.2004 to 27.06.2006 and on 27.06.2006, the age of the accused was more than 18 years of age.
The learned court thereafter rejected the petition filed by the petitioner.

6. This Court has gone through the impugned order and finds that the court has considered the specific case of the petitioner by taking his date of birth as 05.01.1988. and has passed the impugned order.
In such circumstances, there was no question of any further inquiry with regard to declaring the petitioner as juvenile.
The court has recorded that on the last date of commission of offence, the petitioner had already crossed 18 years 6 months as per the date of birth claimed by the petitioner.
This Court finds no illegality or perversity in the impugned order, and therefore, the impugned order does not call for any interference.
This criminal revision is accordingly dismissed.
7. Let a copy of this order be communicated to the court concerned through FAX/email.
